No survey-quality levels are published, so none are drawn | 9Shafts: King's Chamber 32.5° north (doglegged) and 45° south, both reaching the outside; the Queen's Chamber pair are sealed and never did | 10North Face Corridor: 9.06 ± 0.07 m, found 2023 | 11Big Void: 2017; minimum 30 m, position approximate Sources: Petrie 1883 · Cole 1925 · Dash & Paulson, JEA 102 (201

chunks.heading: Figure: Göbekli Tepe, Enclosure D: plan
chunks.text: The diameter is the number most often got wrong. “20 m” circulates widely; it descends from Schmidt's general statement that Layer III enclosures range 10–30 m across. The only published measured plan analysis gives a maximum inner diameter of about 14 m, which is what is drawn. No azimuth is marked, and the omission is the point: the alignment figures in circulation come from papers the excavation team has publicly rejected, and there is no survey-published value to draw instead. The wall plaster dates to 9745–9314 cal BC, which dates a plaster surface, not the raising of the pillars. The enclosure is now understood to be multi-phase, and the fills that were once read as ritual backfill are now read as settlement deposits that slipped in. Key: 1Inner wall: maximum inner diameter about 14 m | 2Eleven peripheral T-pillars, 3–4 m tall, set into the wall with their broad faces turned inward | 3Two central pillars: about 5.5 m tall and 8 t, 2.8 m apart between their inner faces | 4Continuous stone bench along the inner wall face Sources: Haklay & Gopher, Camb. Archaeol. J. 30 (2020) · Dietrich et al., DAI radiocarbon sequence · Clare, e-Forschungsberichte des DAI (2020)

chunks.heading: Figure: Stonehenge: enclosure and stone settings
chunks.text: Overall dimensions are survey figures; the spacing of individual trilithons and bluestones is generalised, and the drawing says so rather than implying a precision it does not have. The axis is marked ≈50° / 230° and no finer, because the only precise historical value in print is Lockyer's 1901 azimuth, which was computed backwards to force a date. The Altar Stone lies flat because the 2024 provenance paper states that whether it ever stood upright is unclear. That paper matched it to the Orcadian Basin of north-east Scotland: a basin, not a quarry, at least 750 km away, and it declined to name a source or to call the transport route demonstrated. chunks.heading: Figure: Megalith heights, to a common scale
chunks.text: Heights are published values; the outlines are generalised, because a silhouette is not a survey. The buried 2.4 m of Stone 56 is drawn because the visible 6.7 m is the figure usually quoted and the 9.1 m total is what the builders actually had to move. Scale comparison is where much of the overstatement in this subject enters: these are large objects, and they are large in ways the experimental and ethnographic record can account for, which is a more interesting fact about people than the alternative. Sources: Darvill et al., Antiquity 86 (2012) · DAI Göbekli Tepe project · Karul, Türk Arkeoloji ve Etnografya Dergisi (2021)

chunks.heading: Figure: Sea level since the Last Glacial Maximum
chunks.text: The lowstand, the timing and rate of Meltwater Pulse 1A, and the 8.2 ka end of the main deglaciation are firm. The depths between the anchors are read off published curves; they are interpolations, not quoted data points, and a reader entitled to the difference should have it. MWP-1B is a shaded box rather than a step because drawing it as a step would settle a dispute the evidence does not settle. This matters here more than usual: a sudden metres-scale rise is exactly what a flood tradition would need, which is precisely why it should not be drawn more firmly than it is known. Key: 1Lowstand: −134 m, sustained 29–21 ka | 2Meltwater Pulse 1A: 14–18 m in 340 years or less, at more than 40 mm/yr, coeval with the Bølling warming | 3Younger Dryas: reduced rates, 12.9–11.7 ka | 4Meltwater Pulse 1B: contested. Present in the Barbados corals, absent from Tahiti and from Lambeck's global reconstruction; published magnitudes run from about zero to 13 m | 5Main deglaciation ends ~8.2 ka; near present level by ~6.7 ka Sources: Deschamps et al., Nature 483 (2012) · Lambeck et al., PNAS 111 (2014) · Bard, Hamelin & Delanghe-Sabatier, Science 327 (2010) · Abdul et al., Paleoceanography 31 (2016)

chunks.heading: Figure: Two proxies, one transition: the end of the Younger Dryas
chunks.text: This figure exists to correct a mistake this site made in an earlier draft. The famous “one to three years” is the deuterium excess, and it is not a temperature. Quoting it as one produces a claim (Greenland warming ten degrees in three years), that the source paper does not make. The two transitions also behaved differently: at the Bølling onset the temperature change was itself fast; at the Younger Dryas termination it was not. Trace shapes here are schematic. The durations, the boundary date and the magnitude are published values. Key: 1Deuterium excess shifts in 1–3 years. This is a moisture-source proxy; it records the North Atlantic storm track reorganising, not a thermometer | 2The Greenland temperature signal follows over about 50–60 years. Magnitude +10 ± 4 °C, from gas isotopes, physically independent of the water-isotope thermometer Sources: Steffensen et al., Science 321 (2008) · Rasmussen et al., JGR 111 (2006) · Grachev & Severinghaus, QSR 24 (2005) · Buizert et al., Science 345 (2014)

chunks.heading: Figure: Where the compared records come from
chunks.text: Coordinates are representative, not exhaustive: a tradition is not a point. The map is here because the clustering is itself a finding, and an inconvenient one. Six of the nine traditions sit within a few weeks' travel of one another and were demonstrably in contact. That makes them poor independent witnesses. Recurrence across neighbours establishes transmission at least as easily as it establishes a shared event: and the two outliers, the Andes and Aboriginal Australia, are doing most of the comparative work precisely because they are far away. Sources: Coastlines from Natural Earth 1:110m, public domain

chunks.heading: Figure: Antikythera mechanism: dial layout
chunks.text: Included as an honest contrast. This is what a genuinely anomalous object looks like when it is real: 82 fragments, 30 surviving gears, tooth counts that can be read (the largest, 223) inscriptions that name the cycles, and a wreck that dates the deposition to about 70–60 BC. It requires no lost civilisation. It requires Hellenistic astronomy, for which there is abundant independent evidence. The 2021 reconstruction's reading of the Venus and Saturn period relations off the cover inscription is well founded; the planetary gear trains it proposes are a hypothesis, with no surviving evidence for most of them. Ring proportions here are schematic; the counts, cycles and dimensions are published. Key: 1Calendar ring: 354 or 355 holes on a ring of 77.1 mm radius, argued statistically in 2024. That implies a Greek lunar year, not the Egyptian 365-day year | 2Zodiac ring, twelve divisions, with solar and lunar pointers | 3Moon-phase display: a half-silvered ball driven by a pin-and-slot device that mechanises the lunar anomaly | 4Metonic dial: 235 synodic months on a five-turn spiral, with Callippic (76 yr) and Games (4 yr) subsidiaries | 5Saros dial: 223 months on a four-turn spiral carrying eclipse glyphs, with the Exeligmos (54 yr) subsidiary Sources: Freeth et al., Nature 444 (2006) · Freeth et al., Nature 454 (2008) · Freeth et al., Sci. Rep. 11 (2021) · Woan & Bayley, Horological J. (2024)

chunks.heading: Figure: How evidence and agreement combine into a rating
chunks.text: Adapted from the calibrated-language approach used in IPCC assessment reports. Two axes, nine cells, four words. No number is attached, because attaching one would imply a calculation that was never performed. A reading moves when the evidence improves or the field converges, and it can move down, which is the part that makes the scale worth having. Sources: After Mastrandrea et al., IPCC guidance note on consistent treatment of uncertainties (2010)

chunks.heading: Evidence cluster: Conscious non-human agency behind anomalous encounter phenomena
chunks.text: Rating: very low. Basis: Structural parallels are established; the inference from them to a persisting external agency is made by no scholar who established them. The effective comparative sample is under four independent witnesses, not ten. The modern instrumental record contains a small genuinely unresolved residue and no physical evidence.. This is the lowest rating on the site, and it is applied to a reading the site takes seriously enough to have spent this much space on. Those two facts are compatible. The material is worth cataloguing because the experiences are real, common, and were dismissed for a century by people who had not looked. The rating is very low because between a real experience and a real entity there is an inferential step, and nothing in the record takes it.

chunks.heading: The claim, stated at full strength
chunks.text: A portion of what is reported as anomalous (lights that behave wrongly, figures at the bedside, encounters that leave a witness certain and a record empty) is caused by conscious beings that are not human and not visible under ordinary conditions. Traditions across the world have described such beings for as long as they have written anything down. If those descriptions are reports rather than inventions, then the modern record and the old one are the same phenomenon under two vocabularies, and the discontinuity we perceive between them is an artefact of our own period's assumption that the question was settled.

chunks.heading: Four claims that are routinely run together
chunks.text: Keeping these apart is the whole discipline of this page. Popular treatments use A to smuggle in C, and cite B as the bridge. B does not bridge; it points the other way.

chunks.heading: What is actually unresolved
chunks.text: Begin with the modern record, because it is the part that can be checked, and because both of the usual summaries of it are wrong. The United States now runs a standing office for this. Its numbers are public and they are specific. In the fiscal year 2024 reporting period the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office received 757 reports . It resolved 49 during the period and recommended a further 243 for closure: balloons, birds, drones, satellites, aircraft. Twenty-one were judged to merit further analysis. And 444 were placed in an archive . Those four numbers sum to 757 exactly, which is worth noting in a literature where figures are usually quoted loosely. The 444 are the ones that get counted as unexplained. The office's own definition of that category is the single most important sentence in this chapter: cases with insufficient data to assess whether the performance characteristics of the underlying event are consistent with those of natural phenomena or exceed the known state-of-the-art. That is a statement about the record, not about the object. A case enters the archive because there was not enough information to analyse it: not because analysis was performed and failed. So hundreds of cases defy explanation inflates it. But everything has been explained is not claimed by anyone at the office either, and the honest middle is narrower and more interesting than either. Its first director put the genuinely anomalous fraction at less than single-digit percentages of the dat

chunks.heading: Three videos, three different answers
chunks.text: The three US Navy infrared clips released in 2020 are usually cited as a set. They have not aged as a set, and the differences are instructive about what resolution actually looks like. GOFAST is resolved. A published case-resolution report reconstructed the aircraft's flight path and modelled the winds: the object was at about 13,000 feet, and once its motion is corrected for wind its intrinsic speed falls between roughly 5 and 92 mph. The dramatic apparent velocity is motion parallax. The report's conclusion, at high confidence, is that the object did not demonstrate anomalous performance characteristics. The popular reading, something screaming just above the waves, is simply wrong, and it is still repeated weekly. FLIR1 is partly resolved. The apparent instantaneous acceleration at the end of the clip coincides with the camera stepping from 1× to 2× zoom and losing track. That specific point is robust and largely uncontested. What the object was remains open. GIMBAL is genuinely unresolved and actively contested. One analysis holds that the object is infrared glare from a distant aircraft and that its apparent rotation is an artefact of the camera's own derotation mechanism. A rebuttal reconstructs flight paths consistent with the aircrew's stated range and finds a solution in which the object decelerates and reverses. Everything turns on the true range, which the released video does not determine. Neither side has closed it, and no official resolution has been published.

chunks.heading: What was, and was not, found in the archives
chunks.text: In March 2024 the same office published a historical review covering 1945 to 2023: roughly two dozen prior programmes, and about thirty interviews with people claiming knowledge of recovered off-world technology. Its findings were unambiguous: no empirical evidence for claims that the USG and private companies have been reverse-engineering extraterrestrial technology , and the alleged programmes named by interviewees either did not exist, were misidentified authentic classified programmes, or resolved to a proposal that was rejected and never established. A physical sample submitted as debris from a crashed craft proved to be a manufactured, terrestrial alloy. Two qualifications, and the site would be dishonest without both. First, the review contains straightforward factual errors: a senator's home state, a sighting date off by a day, an investigator's name, a project's designation. None touches the central finding, but they are the kind of error that tells you how carefully the surrounding text was checked. And structurally, an assessment built on interviews and archival review cannot prove that no compartmented programme exists. Found no evidence means exactly that. Second, and more interesting: the review's own work surfaced a programme that cuts the other way. Reporting in 2025 described a decades-long practice in which personnel in classified units were shown images of flying saucers, told they were part of a recovery programme, made to sign non-disclosure agreements, a

chunks.heading: The parallel is real
chunks.text: Now the part that is genuinely strong, and that sceptical writing tends to skip. The observation that modern encounter reports rhyme with older folk encounter traditions is not an enthusiast's conceit. It was made carefully, by trained folklorists, in peer-reviewed venues, and it has survived. Thomas E. Bullard's comparative analysis of abduction narratives found that across 193 multi-episode cases the reported sequence of events conformed to a single structure in roughly 84 per cent of instances: capture, examination, conference, tour, return, aftermath, in that order. Peter Rojcewicz mapped the Men in Black encounter onto older demonological visitation traditions in the Journal of American Folklore . The motifs Vallée catalogued in 1969 (paralysis, missing time, small humanoid figures, luminosity, distorted time-sense, taboos on food offered, gifts that prove worthless) are the standing furniture of European fairy tradition, and they are also what abduction accounts report. Alongside this sits the strongest empirical result in the whole literature, and it belongs to David Hufford. Folklore studies had long assumed a cultural source hypothesis : the tradition generates the report, so an account's content is explained by what the informant had already heard. Hufford's fieldwork in Newfoundland on the Old Hag broke that assumption. He found accounts richer in detail than the local tradition encoded; he found the same experience in people with no exposure to the tradition at al

chunks.heading: And it points the other way
chunks.text: Here is where this wing has to be careful, because the finding above is routinely recruited to support a conclusion it does not support, and the person doing the recruiting is usually not being dishonest, only fast. Hufford's own model has two parts: a biologically fixed experiential core, and a culturally supplied identification. His fifth proposition states it outright: culture determines the description and the interpretation, not the experience . He is explicit about where he stops. He argues that the experience is real, that a spiritual interpretation of it is rational for the person who had it, and that nothing in current science rules that interpretation out. He does not argue that the beings exist. He says the hypothesis leaves open the question of the nature of the phenomena experienced. Apply his model to the case at hand. The stable core (paralysis, a sensed presence, pressure on the chest, terror, figures at the bedside, distorted time) is stable because it is neurophysiological. The content: Old Hag, incubus, kanashibari , pandafeche , grey alien: is supplied by whatever the local symbolic economy has to hand. On Hufford's own account, the continuity between the fairy encounter and the abduction report is evidence for a shared substrate and against a shared agency , because the identity of the agent is precisely the term that varies. This is the hinge of the whole wing, so it is worth stating without hedging. The continuity is real, and it is real at the level of

chunks.heading: The costume changes
chunks.text: A second line of evidence points the same way, and it is almost embarrassingly regular. In 1896 and 1897 the United States reported airships: cigar-shaped hulls with propellers, searchlights and human crews, at a moment when powered flight was expected imminently and had not yet happened. One witness described the craft as pedal-powered. In 1944 and 1945 aircrew on both sides of the war reported glowing spheres pacing their aircraft, and each side assumed the other had built them; neither had. In 1946 Scandinavia reported rocket-shaped objects and assumed captured V-2s; thirty recovered fragments proved to be meteorite, coke and slag. In June 1947 a pilot described nine objects moving like a saucer if you skip it across the water (a simile about motion, and his own drawings show a crescent) a wire service printed the shape rather than the motion, and within a fortnight the country was reporting discs. Black triangles rise in the window when the F-117 and B-2 make faceted and flying-wing planforms public. In the winter of 2024 the reports were quadcopters. Five repetitions, each independently documented. It is the strongest single argument that the reported form of these objects is culturally supplied. Its reach should be stated exactly. It establishes that morphology tracks expectation. It does not establish that nothing was seen. chunks.heading: What the traditions actually say
chunks.text: The comparison below names traditions directly. That is a change from how the rest of this site is written, and it is made here because the alternative was worse: a comparative table with a conspicuous hole in it where the best-documented material sits. Four things have to be got right, and popular treatments get all four wrong. Category. In the Islamic tradition, belief in angels is one of the six articles of faith, and the jinn are affirmed by explicit Quranic text including an entire sura named for them. This is creed, not custom. Describing it as folklore is a category error that no Muslim scholar would recognise, and this page does not make it. The English genie , a lamp-dwelling wish-granter, is an eighteenth-century French confection and has nothing to do with the subject. Aerial connection. There is one, it is textually explicit, and it is not the one modern claimants reach for. The Quran describes shayatin attempting to ascend to overhear the celestial assembly and being driven off by piercing flames, the shihab , the meteor. That is a genuine seventh-century association between non-human beings and an aerial phenomenon, and it belongs in the table. What the classical sources do not contain is any notion of these beings as pilots of structured craft. They are associated overwhelmingly with terrestrial places: wastes and ruins, wells, thresholds, marketplaces, burial grounds. chunks.heading: Ten traditions, fewer than four witnesses
chunks.text: The comparison has one further problem, and it is arithmetical rather than interpretive. A ten-row table looks like ten independent confirmations. It is not. Mesopotamian demonology reaches Greece in the orientalising period and Judaism during the exile; Christianity inherits it directly; Roman demonology is Greek philosophy in Latin; Islamic angelology shares the Late Antique Near Eastern milieu, with Jibril and Mikal recognisably the Gabriel and Michael of the neighbouring traditions. The Norse and Irish records exist only because Christian monks wrote them down, two centuries or more after conversion. That is one witness, counted eight times. Two genuine exceptions. The jinn specifically have pre-Islamic Arabian attestation independent of the Christian demonological stream, the ginnaye of Palmyrene inscriptions from the first three centuries, and pre-Islamic poetry. And the Andean and Australian traditions were genuinely outside the Old World stream, the latter for something over fifty thousand years. The structural irony is worth naming. Independence and documentation quality are inversely correlated across this entire dataset. The best-documented traditions are the least independent of one another, precisely because they belong to a single literate complex that spent three thousand years translating and arguing with itself. chunks.heading: Why convergence is not evidence here
chunks.text: The reading under examination rests on an inference: many traditions independently describe such beings, therefore such beings probably exist. The inference fails, for reasons worth setting out because they are not merely sceptical reflex. The convergence is thin where it counts. There exist non-human intelligent agents is close to entailed by having a theory of mind and living in an uncertain world. The details are what would evidence a shared referent, and the details diverge sharply and in ways that track local ecology and social structure. Compare the sun: cross-cultural agreement on the sun comes with massive agreement about the particulars: bright, hot, one, high, moving, absent at night. That is what convergence looks like when there is something out there. Agreement on there are unseen persons with almost no agreement below it is what convergence looks like when the referent is cognitive. There is an adequate common cause that is not the referent, and it also explains the divergence. Shared cognitive architecture, shared physiology, and shared social problems predict both the recurrence and the variation. The shared-referent hypothesis explains the recurrence and has no account of the variation: it must treat the wild differences as noise, and there is far more noise than signal. chunks.heading: What would change this rating
chunks.text: A reading that cannot say what would move it is not a reading. Four things would, in ascending order of force. Instrumented data of the quality the phenomenon is claimed to have. Calibrated multi-sensor observation, published with metadata, showing a single object under simultaneous independent instruments performing outside the known envelope. Every serious body examining this identifies data quality, not analytic technique, as the binding constraint. This is a solvable engineering problem and it has not been solved. An encounter phenomenology that resists cultural tracking. The costume argument would be broken by a wave whose reported form does not resemble the technology of its moment. Five waves have now tracked; a sixth that did not would be a genuine result. Structural detail converging where physiology does not constrain it. Hufford's finding is powerful precisely because the invariant features are the ones a neurophysiological account predicts. Convergence on specifics that physiology does not predict (and that transmission cannot explain, in populations with documented non-contact) would be evidence of a different kind. Bullard's consistency finding also still lacks its control: no corpus of invented narratives has been scored on the same taxonomy, so more consistent than folklore should be remains a claim about an unmeasured baseline. chunks.text: Read this first. This wing names living religious traditions directly, which the rest of the site does not.
